'''USS ''Springfield'' (SSN-761)''', a {{sclass|Los Angeles|submarine}}, is the fourth ship of the [[United States Navy]] to bear the name. The boat was named in honor of both the cities of [[Springfield, Illinois]] and [[Springfield, Massachusetts]].

The contract to build her was awarded to the [[Electric Boat Division]] of [[General Dynamics Corporation]] in [[Groton, Connecticut]] on 21 March 1986, and her keel was [[keel laying|laid down]] on 29 January 1990. She was [[ship naming and launching|launched]] on 4 January 1992 sponsored by [[Lynn Morley Martin|Lynn Martin]], and [[ship commissioning|commissioned]] on 9 January 1993.  ''Springfield'' is homeported at [[Naval Base Guam]] in [[Agana, Guam]] and is assigned to Submarine Squadron FIFTEEN.

In mid-2004, ''Springfield'' began an extensive overhaul, or Depot Modernization Period (DMP), at the [[Electric Boat]] shipyard in Groton. In addition to normal periodic maintenance and repairs, ''Springfield'' received extensive modernization in fire control systems, [[sonar]] processing, weapons launch systems, and communications outfit, a [[ring laser gyro]] inertial navigation system, as well as stealth improvements and engine room upgrades.  The modernization was the first major overhaul and repair job for Electric Boat in almost 25 years.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nstcenter.org/docs/PDFs/MR2006_Fleet_004SkipCastroFleetForces.pdf |title=Electric Boat Paint Process Transformation }}{{dead link |date=June 2013}}</ref> Originally awarded as a 12 month, $26.3 million depot modernization,<ref>{{cite press release|title=Navy awards EB $10M for submarine maintenance planning |publisher=[[Electric Boat|General Dynamics Electric Boat Corporation]] |date=26 September 2003 |url=http://www.gdeb.com/news/2003archives.html#09-26-03 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080706165152/http://www.gdeb.com/news/2003archives.html |archive-date=6 July 2008 }}</ref> ''Springfield'' was to be the test case for the possibility of awarding future repair and overhaul contracts to Electric Boat. The overhaul was plagued by cost and time overruns, and when finally completed in December 2005, it was several months late and well over budget. Electric Boat has not been awarded any DMP contracts since.

''Springfield'' arrived at PNSY on 1 December 2016 to begin an Engineering Overhaul. ''Springfield'' will undergo planned maintenance work and system certifications primarily focused on modernizing systems associated with the boat's engine room.<ref name=":0">{{Cite news|url=http://www.seacoastonline.com/news/20161201/uss-springfield-arrives-at-portsmouth-naval-shipyard|title=USS Springfield arrives at Portsmouth Naval Shipyard|first=Brian|last=Early|work=seacoastonline.com|access-date=2017-05-16|language=en}}</ref>

''Springfield'' transferred homeports from Pearl Harbor to Naval Base Guam on March 21, 2022. <ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.dvidshub.net/news/416972/uss-springfield-arrives-guam|title = USS Springfield Arrives in Guam}}</ref>

== Awards ==
''Springfield'' has deployed overseas on many occasions and earned several [[Meritorious Unit Commendation]]s and [[Battle E|Battle "E"]] Efficiency awards.

In 1998, ''Springfield'' won the Captain Edward F. Ney Silver Cup Trophy for outstanding food service (first place in the submarine category). The Ney Memorial Awards, presented annually to the top Navy galleys in ten categories, were established by the Secretary of the Navy and the International Food Service Executives Association (IFSEA) in 1958.<ref>{{cite press release | title = Navy and Marine Corps food service award winners announced |publisher=Navy News Wire |date=5 February 1998}} Quoted in {{cite web |title=Navy and Marine Corps food service award winners announced |website=SeabeeCook.com |publisher=SeabeeCook Publishing |date=27 July 1999 |url=http://www.seabeecook.com/today/news/archive.01/cook0041.htm |access-date=2009-06-21}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |author=International Food Service Executives Association |title=Military Awards Overview by Military Branch |url=http://www.ifsea.com/military_inside.cfm?itemid=14310&catid=2304 |access-date=2009-06-21 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110713004339/http://www.ifsea.com/military_inside.cfm?itemid=14310&catid=2304 |archive-date=13 July 2011 |url-status=dead |df=dmy-all }}</ref>

In 2002 the boat received the [[Arleigh Burke]] Fleet Trophy for most improved ship in the Atlantic Fleet,<ref>{{cite press release |title=Captain Daniel P. Forney, U.S. Navy |publisher=Public Affairs Office, Naval Submarine School |date=6 September 2007 |url=https://www.netc.navy.mil/centers/slc/nss/forney.htm }}{{dead link|date=April 2025|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Springfield wins Arleigh Burke Award |work=The Dolphin |place=Groton, Connecticut |publisher=Journal Register Company |date=10 July 2003 |url=http://www.zwire.com/site/index.cfm?newsid=9497176 }}{{dead link|date=December 2017 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>{{failed verification |date=June 2013}}<ref>{{cite news |title=Bravo Zulu Springfield |work=The Dolphin |place=Groton, Connecticut |publisher=Journal Register Company |date=11 December 2003 |url=http://www.zwire.com/site/index.cfm?newsid=10641115 }}{{dead link|date=December 2017 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>{{failed verification |date=June 2013}} while under command of Commander D.P. Forney.

In 2003 the boat was awarded the Retention Excellence Award for her squadron.<ref>{{cite news |last=Savage |first=Mark A. |title=NSSC Receives Fiscal Year '03 Retention Excellence Award |work=Navy News Service |date=1 March 2004 |url=http://www.navy.mil/search/display.asp?story_id=12051 |access-date=22 June 2009 |archive-date=13 September 2007 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070913012910/https://www.navy.mil/search/display.asp?story_id=12051 |url-status=dead }}</ref> She has also won multiple awards for Navigation, Engineering, Medical, Supply, Damage Control and Deck Seamanship excellence in various years.
